gap: No result ChatGPT got states, across brands, that a '4K' DVR records 4K coax cameras at only 7–15 fps per channel: Viewtron VT-DVR-8 does 7 fps at 4K/8MP, and Dahua XVR7208A-4K-I3 does 15 fps on TVI and AHD. Dahua's 30 fps at 4K needs CVI cameras and Encode Enhancement turned on, and covers only channels 1 and 5. Older CVBS cameras stay at 960H on any of these recorders.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Dahua XVR7208A-4K-I3 product page, the cited Hikvision DS-7208HQHI-S1/XT page and the cited Dahua XVR7108HE-4K-I3 datasheet. The Dahua product pages do list their own limits in the spec tab: 'TVI: 4K@15 fps' and 'the 1st, 5th channel 4K@(1 fps–30 fps), others 4K@(1 fps–15 fps)' when Encode Enhancement is on. That part of the finding is already in a cited rival. None of the results compares across brands. None gives Viewtron's 7 fps at 4K. ChatGPT's answer said only 'up to 4K recording', with no frame rate, and the Dahua key point reads 'Max. 4K@30fps Encoding Capability' with no caveat. The Hikvision page loaded empty, so I couldn't check it.
decides: The footnote changes the pick by camera type. If the shopper's coax cameras are 1080p or older CVBS, every candidate records them at full frame rate, and Viewtron lists CVBS only up to 960H. Paying for a '4K' DVR (Viewtron at $799.99, Dahua 7208A) gains them nothing, so a cheaper 1080p or 5 MP hybrid such as the ZOSI ZR08VMA or ANNKE DR85 is the logical buy. Only owners of real 4K coax cameras should pay for 4K, and then the camera format matters. Dahua with HD-CVI cameras gets 30 fps on two channels (with Encode Enhancement on); TVI or AHD cameras get 15 fps on Dahua and 7 fps on Viewtron. For motion such as faces or plates, 7 fps at 4K is worse than 30 fps at 1080p. Our page's 'TVI up to 4K' cell for Viewtron should carry the fps.

findings.label: Top analog input by coax format
findings.value: CVI 4K at 25/30 fps; TVI 4K at 15 fps; AHD 4K at 15 fps; no CVBS resolution listed
findings.source_title: XVR7208A-4K-I3 8-Channel Penta-brid 4K WizSense DVR - Zhejiang Dahua Technology Co., Ltd.
findings.note: Quoted from the spec list: '1. CVI: 4K@25/30 fps…', '2. TVI: 4K@15 fps; 5 MP(2560 x 1944)@20 fps', '3. AHD: 4K@15 fps; 5 MP@20 fps; 4 MP@25/30 fps'. The 8 BNC ports auto-detect HDCVI, AHD, TVI and CVBS.

findings.label: 4K main-stream recording frame rate
findings.value: 4K at 1–15 fps per channel by default; 4K at up to 30 fps only on channels 1 and 5, and only with Encode Enhancement on
findings.source_title: XVR7208A-4K-I3 8-Channel Penta-brid 4K WizSense DVR - Zhejiang Dahua Technology Co., Ltd.
findings.note: The key-points headline says 'Max. 4K@30fps Encoding Capability'. The spec tab limits that to channels 1 and 5. With Encode Enhancement on, EPTZ, face recognition, perimeter protection and other analytics are disabled. 6 MP records at up to 20 fps, and 5 MP and below at 25/30 fps.

findings.label: IP channels and storage
findings.value: Up to 16 IP channels: 8 by default plus 8 more by converting analog channels to IP; 2 SATA bays, up to 16 TB each
findings.source_title: XVR7208A-4K-I3 8-Channel Penta-brid 4K WizSense DVR - Zhejiang Dahua Technology Co., Ltd.
findings.note: '8 IP channels by default + 8 channels (analog channels are converted to IP channels)'. Dahua says the per-disk limit 'varies depending on the environment temperature'. Turning on IP extension disables SMD, perimeter protection and other analytics.

findings.label: 4K recording frame rate, IP channels and storage
findings.value: Same per-format limits as the 7208A: TVI and AHD 4K at 15 fps, CVI 4K at 25/30 fps, 4K at 30 fps only on channels 1 and 5 with Encode Enhancement; up to 16 IP channels (8 converted from analog); 1 SATA bay, up to 16 TB
findings.source_title: XVR7108HE-4K-I3 - Zhejiang Dahua Technology Co., Ltd.
findings.note: This is the product page for the model ChatGPT cited by datasheet. The 1-bay chassis is the only spec difference from the 7208A that I confirmed.

findings.label: Recording frame rate per camera, BNC inputs
findings.value: 30 fps at 960H/720p/1080p; 15 fps at 4 MP; 12 fps at 5 MP; 7 fps at 4K/8 MP
findings.note: From the spec list: '7 FPS per camera @ 4K / 8mp'. The page's headline summary says '8fps@4K', so the page contradicts itself. I use the spec-list figure. IP cameras record at 30 fps up to 4K/8 MP.

findings.label: Resolution by coax format
findings.value: CVBS: CIF, D1, 960H only; AHD, HD-TVI and HD-CVI: 720p up to 8 MP/4K
findings.note: This confirms that older CVBS cameras top out at 960H even on a 4K recorder.

findings.label: Price, drive, IP channels
findings.value: $799.99 sale ($899.99 list) at CCTV Camera Pros; 2 bays, 12 TB each (24 TB total); 8 IP channels (16 total); NDAA compliant
findings.note: The included drive is stated two ways on the same page: '2TB Video Hard Drive' in the purchase section and '1TB Hard Drive Included' in the spec list. Our current page says 2 TB, so this needs checking before publishing.
